question: Two pipes, A and B, can fill a tank of 3700 litres in 9 hours and 6 hours, respectively. If they are opened together, how many hours will they take to fill an empty tank of 6400 litres?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency of **Pipe A** = 3700 ÷ 9 litres/hr.

Efficiency of **Pipe B** = 3700 ÷ 6 litres/hr.

Combined efficiency = (3700 × (2 + 3)) ÷ 18 = (3700 × 5) ÷ 18 = 18500 ÷ 18 = 9250 ÷ 9 litres/hr.

Time to fill 6400 litres = 6400 ÷ (9250 ÷ 9) = (6400 × 9) ÷ 9250 = (640 × 9) ÷ 925 = 1152 ÷ 185 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 1152/185 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Total Capacity** of target tank = 6400 litres.

⇒ Efficiency of **Pipe A** (EA) = 3700/9 litres/hr.

⇒ Efficiency of **Pipe B** (EB) = 3700/6 = 1850/3 litres/hr.

⇒ Combined Efficiency (EA₊B) = (3700/9) + (1850/3) = (3700 + 5550)/9 = 9250/9 litres/hr.

⇒ Time taken = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time = 6400 ÷ (9250/9) = (6400 × 9) ÷ 9250

⇒ Time = (640 × 9) ÷ 925 = 5760 ÷ 925

⇒ Time = 1152/185 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 1152/185 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Combined Efficiency Formula

When two pipes work together, their **total efficiency** is the sum of their individual efficiencies: Eₜₒₜₐₗ = E₁ + E₂.

Time and Work Relationship

The **time** taken to complete a task is inversely proportional to the **efficiency**: Time = Total Work ÷ Efficiency.

Inlet vs Outlet Pipes

**Inlet pipes** have positive efficiency (add water), while **outlet pipes** (leaks) have negative efficiency (remove water).</p
